description: Blue Team Village at DEF CON 30 focuses on digital forensics, incident response, threat hunting tradecraft, malware reverse engineering, and defensive tooling.

talks.title: YARA Rules to Rule Them All
talks.teaser: Saurabh Chaudhary demonstrates crafting high-performance, modular YARA rules to detect complex malware variants and streamline threat hunting.

talks.title: Threat Hunt Trilogy: A Beast in the Shadow
talks.teaser: Meisam Eslahi presents advanced threat hunting tradecraft to track stealthy adversaries lurking across enterprise infrastructure.
talks.summary:
In this presentation at the DEF CON 30 Blue Team Village, cybersecurity researcher Meisam Eslahi presents "Threat Hunt Trilogy: A Beast in the Shadow," detailing a disciplined forensic methodology for identifying hidden adversaries within compromised enterprise networks. He opens at 09:00 by detailing the continuous threat hunting loop, stressing that analysts must systematically review, improve, document, and update detection logic with each investigation.

Meisam explores detecting destructive malware at 18:00, explaining how anomalous mass-file modification behavior serves as a high-fidelity indicator of active ransomware or disk-wiping payloads. At 27:00, he demonstrates live host triage techniques, examining running process hierarchies, active file descriptors, and open network sockets to detect anomalous execution trees.

Transitioning to deep memory forensics at 36:00, Meisam showcases using Volatility 3 plugins like netscan to uncover covert command-and-control network sockets hidden from traditional OS diagnostic tools. He correlates these findings with network traffic captures at 45:00, analyzing malicious HTTP beacon intervals to expose stealthy adversary communication channels. He concludes at 54:00 with recommendations for translating hunt findings into durable SIEM correlation rules. (AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: Project Obsidian: Reverse Engineering Malware - Phishing in the Morning & Abundance of Samples
talks.teaser: Project Obsidian walks through triaging and reverse engineering high volumes of malicious email attachments and phishing lures.

talks.title: Project Obsidian: Reverse Engineering Malware - Analyzing Obfuscated PowerShell
talks.teaser: Project Obsidian explores methods for decoding and analyzing heavily obfuscated PowerShell scripts used in initial access payloads.

talks.title: Project Obsidian: Mise En Place for Incident Investigations
talks.teaser: Project Obsidian explains forensic preparation and tooling organization to accelerate digital forensics and incident triage workflows.

talks.title: Malware Hunting: Discovering Evasive Techniques in PDF Documents
talks.teaser: Filipi Pires demonstrates techniques for dissecting malicious PDF documents, extracting embedded JavaScript, and uncovering hidden exploit streams.
talks.summary:
In this technical workshop at the DEF CON 30 Blue Team Village, security researcher Filipi Pires provides an in-depth breakdown of malicious PDF analysis, examining the evasion techniques employed by threat actors to deliver document-based exploits. He begins at 08:00 by discussing cyber resilience strategies, emphasizing that defensive teams must understand attacker delivery tradecraft to protect enterprise endpoints from weaponized email attachments.

Filipi deconstructs the internal architecture of the PDF specification at 16:00, explaining how objects, dictionaries, streams, and cross-reference (XREF) tables function together. At 24:00, he demonstrates inspecting raw file headers and strings to identify anomalous embedded scripts, followed by using diagnostic tools like PDFiD and pdf-parser at 32:00 to detect suspicious OpenAction triggers and embedded JavaScript.

At 40:00, Filipi analyzes advanced obfuscation methods, showing how attackers nest objects and apply multiple encoding layers (such as FlateDecode and hex encoding) to evade static antivirus scanners. He concludes at 48:00 by demonstrating how to extract and decode raw shellcode payloads from PDF streams, providing guidance on authoring robust YARA detection signatures for SOC and malware analysis teams. (AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: Malicious Memory Techniques on Windows & How to Spot Them
talks.teaser: Connor Morley analyzes Windows in-memory injection techniques—including process hollowing and thread hijacking—and how defenders detect them.

talks.title: Lend Me Your IRs: Effective Incident Response Triage & Telemetry
talks.teaser: Matt Scheurer shares battle-tested incident response methodologies, telemetry sources, and fast containment strategies for enterprise defenders.

talks.title: Project Obsidian: Incident Response OODA Loop - An Hour in an Incident Responder's Life
talks.teaser: Project Obsidian breaks down the Observe-Orient-Decide-Act (OODA) loop applied to real-time incident triage and crisis response.

talks.title: Project Obsidian: Incident Response - Scoping the Incident from the Ground Up
talks.teaser: Project Obsidian details the critical initial phase of incident response: defining the blast radius, scoping compromised systems, and setting containment boundaries.
talks.summary:
In this instructional session from Project Obsidian at the DEF CON 30 Blue Team Village, instructors break down the foundational principles of incident scoping during digital forensics and incident response (DFIR) operations. The presentation opens at 06:00 by defining an incident scope—distinguishing confirmed forensic facts from assumptions and evaluating initial organizational impact across critical business systems.

At 12:00, the speaker emphasizes the necessity of centralizing investigative findings into a shared evidence repository, ensuring all analysts work from a consistent timeline. Guidance on conducting non-adversarial witness and employee interviews follows at 18:00, showing how open-ended questioning uncovers initial infection vectors without inducing defensiveness. At 24:00, the session explores calculating adversary dwell time, contrasting historical industry averages with modern fast-moving ransomware threats.

The talk concludes at 30:00 by illustrating how to structure formal, executive-ready incident reports that clearly communicate containment boundaries and remediation priorities. At 36:00, the speaker addresses the emotional and mental strain of prolonged incident handling, providing practical advice on maintaining investigative rigor and managing team fatigue during high-stress corporate intrusions. (AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: Project Obsidian: Incident Response - Making Final Executive Reporting Exciting
talks.teaser: Project Obsidian shares guidelines for translating complex forensic findings into clear, impactful incident reports for leadership and stakeholders.

talks.title: Securing macOS and Linux Endpoints in Azure Active Directory
talks.teaser: Microsoft Principal Program Manager Mark Morowczynski examines conditional access, identity integration, and posture management for macOS and Linux on Azure AD.

talks.title: Hunting Malicious Office Macros: VBA Deobfuscation & Detection
talks.teaser: Anton Ovrutsky demonstrates behavioral detection patterns, static parsing tools, and deobfuscation methods to hunt malicious Office VBA macros.

talks.title: Horusec: Open-Source Static Application Security Testing for Everyone
talks.teaser: Gilmar Esteves and Filipi Pires present Horusec, an open-source multi-language static analysis (SAST) tool designed to democratize code security scanning.
talks.summary:
In this technical briefing at the DEF CON 30 Blue Team Village, Gilmar Esteves and Filipi Pires introduce Horusec, an open-source multi-language Static Application Security Testing (SAST) platform designed to democratize automated code security analysis. At 03:00, they demonstrate how Horusec parses source code repositories, displaying flagged vulnerabilities with precise file names, line numbers, and severity ratings.

The speakers walk through a practical demonstration environment at 06:00, scanning sample codebases to showcase detection capabilities for SQL injection, cross-site scripting, and hardcoded secrets across multiple languages at 09:00. At 12:00, they showcase the Horusec IDE plugin for Visual Studio Code, highlighting how developers receive real-time security alerts directly in their editor as they write code.

Diving into vulnerability triage at 15:00, they show how Horusec provides contextual remediation advice, CWE links, and false-positive filtering. At 18:00, they illustrate integrating Horusec into automated CI/CD deployment pipelines using lightweight CLI commands and quality gates to block insecure builds before production. They wrap up at 21:00 with project roadmap milestones and an invitation to join the open-source developer community. (AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: Project Obsidian: Using Chainsaw for Rapid Windows Event Log Triage
talks.teaser: Project Obsidian demonstrates using Chainsaw and Sigma rules to rapidly parse gigabytes of Windows event logs and identify malicious artifacts.

talks.title: Project Obsidian: The Importance of Sysmon Telemetry for Investigations
talks.teaser: Project Obsidian details configuring Sysinternals Sysmon to capture critical process creation, network connection, and DLL load events for investigations.

talks.title: Project Obsidian: Kill Chain Endpoint Forensics Walkthrough
talks.teaser: Project Obsidian walks through an end-to-end endpoint forensic investigation, reconstructing attacker actions using MFT, Prefetch, and Shimcache artifacts.

talks.title: Project Obsidian: Creating Custom Velociraptor Artifact Collectors
talks.teaser: Project Obsidian demonstrates writing custom Velociraptor Query Language (VQL) artifacts to hunt for IOCs and collect forensic evidence across thousands of endpoints.
talks.summary:
In this practical forensics lab from Project Obsidian at the DEF CON 30 Blue Team Village, investigators present a step-by-step guide to building custom artifact collectors using the Velociraptor endpoint visibility and response framework. The session begins at 03:00 by demonstrating how to select target forensic artifacts specifically tailored for compromised Linux server environments within the Velociraptor console.

At 06:00, the instructor configures a standalone offline collector binary, walking through artifact definition scripts written in Velociraptor Query Language (VQL) to harvest process tables, persistence hooks, and system logs. The guide demonstrates executing the compiled collector directly on target Linux endpoints at 09:00, highlighting operational privilege requirements and output packaging.

The lab details the process of bundling extracted evidence into compressed triage archives at 12:00. At 15:00, the instructor shows how to import the offline collection back into the central Velociraptor server, demonstrating how security analysts can rapidly run VQL queries across centralized triage data to reconstruct adversary actions without maintaining continuous network connectivity to the target host. (AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: Even My Dad is a Threat Modeler: Demystifying Threat Modeling for Everyone
talks.teaser: Sarthak Taneja presents an accessible, real-world approach to threat modeling, showing how everyday risk intuition translates to software and architecture defense.

talks.title: Project Obsidian: Cyber Threat Intelligence - Generating CTI from Live Incidents
talks.teaser: Project Obsidian explains how to extract actionable cyber threat intelligence, TTPs, and indicator clusters from real-time incident investigations.

talks.title: Project Obsidian: Cyber Threat Hunting - When the Logs Are Gone
talks.teaser: Project Obsidian shows how threat hunters investigate compromises when adversaries clear event logs, leveraging USN journals, volume shadow copies, and memory artifacts.

talks.title: Project Obsidian: Cyber Threat Hunting - Sniffing Out BloodHound in Active Directory
talks.teaser: Project Obsidian demonstrates detecting SharpHound and BloodHound reconnaissance by hunting anomalous LDAP queries and Active Directory enumeration patterns.
talks.summary:
In this threat hunting workshop from Project Obsidian at the DEF CON 30 Blue Team Village, instructors demonstrate how defensive analysts can detect BloodHound and SharpHound reconnaissance activity inside enterprise Active Directory environments. Entering the Splunk hunting lab at 07:00, the session examines event log sources necessary to spot internal domain enumeration.

At 14:00, the instructor investigates host-level telemetry, specifically querying Sysmon Event ID 11 (File Create) to identify telltale SharpHound output files and JSON archive creation artifacts. The workshop shifts to building high-fidelity detection logic at 21:00, writing Splunk search queries that trigger automated SOC alerts whenever suspicious Active Directory data dumping occurs.

Turning to network-based anomalies at 28:00, the presenter identifies unusual spikes in SMB traffic (port 445) and rapid LDAP session queries originating from administrative jump boxes and RDP hosts. The session concludes at 35:00 by showing how to compile forensic findings into a comprehensive threat hunting report, establishing actionable indicators of compromise (IOCs) to thwart adversary privilege escalation paths. (AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: Project Obsidian: Cyber Threat Hunting - Hunting for Adversary Scheduled Tasks & Persistence
talks.teaser: Project Obsidian details hunting for malicious scheduled tasks, cron jobs, and stealthy persistence mechanisms across enterprise endpoints.

talks.title: Project Obsidian: Cyber Threat Hunting - Visualizing Phishing Campaigns & Attack Graphs
talks.teaser: Project Obsidian demonstrates using graph visualization tools to map phishing infrastructure, identify sender anomalies, and correlate multi-stage campaigns.
